articles.title: ASC 944 — Financial Services: Insurance
articles.summary: Top-level US GAAP standard governing insurance accounting. Codifies recognition, measurement, and disclosure for insurance contracts.
articles.body_md:
## ASC 944 in 60 seconds

**Scope.** Applies to entities that issue insurance contracts (life, P&C, health, reinsurance, financial guaranty).

**Key sub-topics.**
- 944-20: Insurance Activities (general)
- 944-30: Acquisition Costs (DAC)
- 944-40: Claim Costs and Liabilities for Future Policy Benefits
- 944-50: Policyholder Dividends
- 944-60: Premium Deficiency and Loss Recognition
- 944-80: Separate Accounts

**ASU 2018-12 (LDTI)** materially changed long-duration contract accounting (effective 2023 for SEC filers): annual assumption review, market-consistent rate for liability for future policy benefits, market risk benefits at fair value, simplified DAC amortization.
articles.gaap_view: Principles-based, going-concern measurement; emphasizes matching of premiums and benefits.
articles.stat_view: Conservative, liquidity/solvency-focused; benefits recognized using statutory mortality/morbidity tables.

articles.title: FAS 60 — Short-Duration Contracts
articles.summary: Original P&C accounting model. Premiums earned over the coverage period; losses recognized as incurred.
articles.body_md:
## Snapshot

**Scope.** Most P&C policies and short-duration health.

**Premium recognition.** Earned ratably over the coverage period (typically 12 months).

**Loss reserves.** Best estimate of unpaid claims (case + IBNR), undiscounted.

**DAC.** Capitalized; amortized in proportion to premium revenue.

**Premium deficiency.** Test at the end of each period — if expected losses + LAE + maintenance > unearned premium, recognize a deficiency.
articles.gaap_view: Undiscounted loss reserves; DAC asset; premium deficiency test.
articles.stat_view: Schedule P loss development; SAP requires full IBNR but with some line-specific conservatism.

articles.title: FAS 97 — Universal Life & Investment Contracts
articles.summary: Establishes account-balance accounting for universal life, deferred annuities, and limited-pay contracts.
articles.body_md:
## Snapshot

**Scope.** Universal life, variable UL, deferred annuities (investment contracts).

**Liability.** Account balance + unearned revenue liability for front-end loads.

**Revenue.** Mortality & expense charges, surrender charges, and investment spread.

**DAC.** Amortized in proportion to estimated gross profits (EGPs) — periodically unlocked.

**Note.** LDTI (ASU 2018-12) simplified DAC amortization to a constant level basis; EGP unlocking is largely retired.
articles.gaap_view: Deposit accounting; revenue from charges; EGP-based DAC (pre-LDTI).
articles.stat_view: Commissioners' Annuity Reserve Valuation Method (CARVM); separate account reporting under SSAP 56.

articles.title: FAS 133 — Derivatives & Hedging (ASC 815)
articles.summary: Governs derivative accounting and hedge designation. Heavily used by life insurers managing interest rate, credit, and equity risk.
articles.body_md:
## Snapshot

**Scope.** All derivatives — futures, swaps, options, embedded derivatives in host contracts.

**Measurement.** Fair value through P&L by default.

**Hedge accounting (optional).**
- Fair value hedge: changes in hedged item & derivative both in P&L
- Cash flow hedge: derivative effective portion in OCI, reclassified when hedged item hits earnings
- Net investment hedge: similar to cash flow hedge for foreign operations

**Insurance relevance.** Variable annuity guarantees (GMxB riders) often contain embedded derivatives bifurcated under ASC 815.
articles.gaap_view: Fair value with optional hedge designation reducing P&L volatility.
articles.stat_view: SSAP 86 — limited hedge accounting; many derivatives carried at amortized cost when used in qualifying hedges.

articles.title: Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP)
articles.summary: Regulator-driven framework focused on solvency and policyholder protection. Codified in NAIC's Accounting Practices & Procedures Manual.
articles.body_md:
## Why two sets of books?

U.S. insurers prepare both **GAAP** (for investors) and **STAT** (for regulators) financials. Statutory accounting is intentionally conservative — it answers *can the company pay claims if it stopped writing tomorrow?*

**Key SAP traits.**
- Non-admitted assets (e.g., furniture, prepaid expenses) excluded from surplus
- DAC is **expensed** when incurred (no GAAP-style asset)
- Investments at amortized cost for high-quality bonds (NAIC 1-2)
- Dividends require regulatory approval if exceeding ordinary thresholds
- Schedules P, F, BA, and D drive risk-based capital (RBC)

**RBC ratio.** Total Adjusted Capital / Authorized Control Level. <200% triggers regulatory action.
articles.stat_view: Liquidation-basis, conservative reserves, non-admitted assets, RBC-driven.

articles.title: LDTI (ASU 2018-12) — Long-Duration Contract Reform
articles.summary: The most significant US GAAP insurance change in decades. Effective 2023 for SEC filers; reshapes life and long-term care reporting.
articles.body_md:
## What changed

1. **LFPB cohorts.** Liability for future policy benefits computed at the issue-year cohort level; assumptions reviewed annually with retrospective unlocking through P&L.
2. **Discount rate.** Upper-medium grade fixed-income yield (single-A-equivalent), updated each period; rate changes flow through OCI.
3. **Market risk benefits (MRBs).** GMxB-type guarantees measured at fair value; non-performance risk in OCI.
4. **DAC.** Amortized on a constant-level basis; no more EGP unlocking.
5. **Disclosures.** Enhanced rollforwards by issue-year cohort.
articles.gaap_view: Annual unlocking, cohort-level LFPB, MRBs at fair value, constant-level DAC.
articles.stat_view: Largely unchanged — SAP retains principle-based reserves (PBR) framework.

articles.title: Combined Ratio — The P&C scoreboard
articles.summary: Combined Ratio = Loss Ratio + Expense Ratio. Below 100% means underwriting profit; above 100% means underwriting loss (offset by investment income).
articles.body_md:
## Formula

```
Loss Ratio       = Incurred Losses & LAE / Earned Premium
Expense Ratio    = Underwriting Expenses / Earned Premium  (GAAP)
                 = Underwriting Expenses / Written Premium (STAT)
Combined Ratio   = Loss Ratio + Expense Ratio
```

## Reading it
- < 95%   = strong underwriting
- 95-100% = profitable
- 100-105% = breakeven; relying on investment income
- > 105%  = underwriting loss; sustainability concern if persistent

## Why GAAP vs STAT differ
GAAP uses earned premium in the denominator of the expense ratio; SAP uses written premium. The two ratios can differ by 1-3 points in a fast-growing book.
articles.stat_view: Written-premium denominator for expense ratio; reported as 'trade ratio' in Schedule P.
